nodes.summary: Backward search always returns a genuine interval of rows, `sp ≤ ep ≤ |L|`, on any list `L` (so the difference in `backwardSearch_count` involves no truncated subtraction).
nodes.title: Backward search returns a genuine row interval

nodes.summary: `ep - sp` is the number of positions `i ≤ |t|` at which `P` occurs in `t`.
nodes.title: Counting occurrences

nodes.summary: Row `r ≤ |t|` lies in the interval `[sp, ep)` computed by backward search on `bwt t` exactly when `P` is a prefix of the suffix of `t` at position `SA[r]`.
nodes.title: Backward-search intervals are suffix-array intervals

nodes.summary: After processing `P`, the interval `[sp, ep)` is exactly the set of rows whose rotation starts with `P`.
nodes.title: Backward search is correct

nodes.summary: FM-index backward search: the half-open row interval `[sp, ep)` for a pattern, computed from the last column alone, processing the pattern from its last letter to its first. The interval for the suffix and `C[c]` are each computed once per letter, so a pattern of length `m` makes `m` recursive calls.
nodes.title: FM-index backward search

nodes.summary: `bwt[r] = t$[SA[r] - 1]`, the letter cyclically before the suffix of row `r` (the sentinel for the row of the whole text, `SA[r] = 0`).
nodes.title: The transform from the suffix array

nodes.summary: The Burrows–Wheeler transform: the last column of the sorted rotation matrix.
nodes.title: Burrows–Wheeler transform

nodes.summary: `C[c]`: the number of letters of `L` smaller than `c`.
nodes.title: Count of smaller letters in the FM-index

nodes.summary: `k` steps of the inversion walk from row `r`: the letters `L[r], L[LF r], …`.
nodes.title: Steps of the Burrows–Wheeler inversion walk

nodes.summary: The Burrows–Wheeler transform is inverted by the LF-mapping walk.
nodes.title: Inversion

nodes.summary: Inversion of the Burrows–Wheeler transform: walk the LF-mapping `|L| - 1` times from row `0` (the rotation that starts with the sentinel) and reverse the letters read.
nodes.title: Inversion of the Burrows–Wheeler transform

nodes.summary: The Burrows–Wheeler transform of `t` has length `|t| + 1` (the sentinel adds one letter).
nodes.title: Length of the Burrows–Wheeler transform

nodes.summary: The LF-mapping computed from the last column alone: `LF(r) = C[L[r]] + rank_{L[r]}(L, r)`.
nodes.title: LF-mapping from the last column

nodes.summary: `k` steps of sampled-suffix-array locate from row `r`: return the stored value of the first sampled row reached along the LF-mapping, plus the number of LF steps taken. `sample r` is the stored value `SA[r]` of row `r`, if any.
nodes.title: Step-bounded sampled-suffix-array locate

nodes.summary: If every stored value is correct (`sample r = some v → v = SA[r]` for rows `r ≤ |t|`) and every row of text position `0` is sampled, then `locate` returns `SA[r]` for every row `r ≤ |t|`.
nodes.title: Sampled-suffix-array locate is correct

nodes.summary: For `0 < s`, if every row whose text position is a multiple of `s` is sampled, then from row `r ≤ |t|` locate makes at most `SA[r] mod s` LF steps (for any amount of fuel `k`). At `s = 0` the `s - 1` bound would be `0` while the proof only gives `SA[r] mod 0 = SA[r]` steps.
nodes.title: Locate takes at most `s - 1` steps

nodes.summary: The number of LF steps `locateAux L sample k r` takes.
nodes.title: Number of LF steps taken by sampled locate

nodes.summary: Sampled-suffix-array locate (Ferragina and Manzini 2000): the text position of row `r` from the last column `L` and the samples, with at most `|L|` LF steps.
nodes.title: Sampled-suffix-array locate

nodes.summary: A sentinel-free word `P` is a prefix of `u ++ ⊥ :: v` (letters lifted to `WithBot α`) exactly when it is a prefix of `u`: the sentinel `⊥` stops every match.
nodes.title: The sentinel stops every prefix match

nodes.summary: `i` is reported for `P` exactly when `i ≤ |t|` and `P` is a prefix of `t.drop i` (the empty pattern occurs at all `|t| + 1` positions).
nodes.title: The reported positions are exactly the occurrences

nodes.summary: The number of reported positions is the length `ep - sp` of the backward-search interval.
nodes.title: Number of FM-index occurrences equals the interval length

nodes.summary: Each occurrence is reported once.
nodes.title: FM-index reports each occurrence once

nodes.summary: The occurrences of `P` reported by the FM-index: the suffix-array entries `SA[sp], …, SA[ep - 1]` of the backward-search interval. The BWT and the interval are bound once with `let` and reused, so one query builds the BWT and runs the backward search once, not three times.
nodes.title: Occurrences of a pattern reported by the FM-index

nodes.summary: The rows of the Burrows–Wheeler matrix are sorted: the rotations listed by `sortedRotations t` are in lexicographically nondecreasing order.
nodes.title: Rows of the Burrows–Wheeler matrix are sorted

nodes.summary: `rank_c(L, r)`: the number of occurrences of `c` among the first `r` letters of `L`.
nodes.title: Rank of a letter in a prefix of the last column

nodes.summary: For `i, j ≤ |t|`, rotation `i` of `withSentinel t` is smaller than rotation `j` exactly when suffix `i` is smaller than suffix `j`.
nodes.title: Rotations of `t$` compare as suffixes

nodes.summary: Sorting the rotations of `withSentinel t` orders the starting positions exactly as sorting its suffixes.
nodes.title: The Burrows–Wheeler matrix is the suffix array of `t$`

nodes.summary: For every row `r`, row `lf (bwt t) r` holds the rotation of row `r` rotated right by one position, i.e. starting one position earlier in the text.
nodes.title: The LF-mapping property

nodes.summary: The starting positions `0, …, |t|` of the rotations of `withSentinel t`, sorted by their rotations in lexicographic order: row `r` of the Burrows–Wheeler matrix is `(withSentinel t).rotate ((sortedRotations t)[r])`.
nodes.title: Sorted rotations of a sentinel-terminated text

nodes.summary: `SA[r] = SA[LF r] + 1` when `SA[r] > 0`.
nodes.title: The LF step moves one position left in the text

nodes.summary: For a row `r ≤ |t|`, `LF r` is a row and `SA[LF r] = SA[r] - 1` cyclically (`SA[LF r] = |t|` when `SA[r] = 0`).
nodes.title: LF in suffix-array terms

nodes.summary: The text `t` with the sentinel `⊥` appended: `t.map (↑) ++ [⊥]`. The sentinel is the unique occurrence of `⊥` and is smaller than every letter.
nodes.title: Text with an appended sentinel

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
